summary: Continued the CI/bootstrap recovery work and pushed the preview compatibility fix further. The repo now has a build-time compatibility shim for SvelteKit preview (`scripts/fix-sveltekit-preview-manifest.mjs`), regression coverage for that shim plus the bootstrap validator, and `service-quote-gates` is wired to run both node-based script tests. The CI-style bootstrap validator still passes when the expected preview artifacts exist, and the earlier incorrect validator requirement on `service-details-visual.spec.ts` remains removed. On this iteration I also narrowed the next real blocker more precisely: preview is no longer failing only on `manifest.js`; the underlying problem is that the local build is not finishing cleanly into a full preview output contract. When inspected between runs, `.svelte-kit/output/` is being cleaned back to empty, `build/` remains stale, and a captured `npm run build` rerun is still only reaching the early Vite/SvelteKit build stages without yet producing `.svelte-kit/output/client` or prerendered output. That means the current repo-side preview fix is in place, but TEST-G3/TEST-G4 browser evidence is still waiting on a successful full build artifact generation path.
remaining_work: Finish diagnosing and fixing the local/CI-shaped build so it completes with the full preview output contract, including `.svelte-kit/output/server`, `.svelte-kit/output/client`, and any required prerendered output alongside `build/`.

Rerun the remaining Chromium and Mobile Safari `service-quotes-*`, `service-ux-hardening*`, `service-instant-buy*`, `homepage-featured-services*`, and `tasks-services-regression-*` suites once the preview artifact contract is fully satisfied.
Run the Chromium visual slice (`service-quotes-visual*`, `homepage-featured-services-visual*`) after the preview output is complete and preview startup is stable.
Finish the remaining `TEST-G3` / `TEST-G4` evidence pass and address any browser-level failures that surface once the full preview output contract is available.

Verify the final `CI-G1` external requirements in the real GitLab environment, including merge-required job behavior and project merge-policy enforcement, once CI runtime variables and project API access are available.
